articles.title: Twitch streamer Bonnie under fire over alleged sexual encounter with a 16-year-old and resurfaced racial slur clips
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Twitch streamer Bonnie has faced a series of online controversies, with resurfaced clips and livestream incidents putting her under intense scrutiny. .
articles.body: Twitch streamer Bonnie has faced a series of online controversies, with resurfaced clips and livestream incidents putting her under intense scrutiny. From a 2014 recording about a sexual encounter to allegations involving a racial slur, the incidents have sparked debate across streaming communities. Bonnie has addressed several claims, while her supporters have also spoken out amid the backlash.Bonnie's 2014 clip sparks controversy over alleged encounterIn April 2026, a 2014 recording of Bonnie discussing a sexual encounter with someone she said was 16 or possibly 17 went viral. The clip triggered widespread criticism and questions about the ages involved.Bonnie later addressed the controversy on Twitch, clarifying that she was 18 when the conversation took place.“Also, I saw a clip going around. I saw an old clip going around, and I just want to make it very, very clear, so that there is absolutely no misinformation or confusion. But that clip, I was 18 in that clip. The clip is from 2014, and you can see the verified dates if you care. So, that's pretty much all there is to it.”The controversy resurfaced in another creator's content when Bradygoo used audio from the clip in a diss track aimed at Arky, Bonnie's frequent streaming collaborator and former OSCS member.The track brought renewed attention to the recording and extended the discussion beyond Bonnie's own audience.Bonnie faces N-word allegations and livestream backlashBonnie also faced allegations of using a racial slur while singing Drake's Marvin's Room during an IRL stream with Cinna. Bonnie denied the accusation, saying she sang the censored lyric instead.“I said 'new guy.' That's what they say in the censored version. He says 'F\*\*k that new guy that you think...' ('Chat, I don't know if Bonnie said it,' said Cinna.)”Cinna defended Bonnie after the incident, saying:“I would never let someone say that around me. She didn't say that word. She didn't say it.”An older, deleted clip allegedly showing Bonnie repeating a racial slur while rapping along to Tyga's Glitta later resurfaced online.During an August 24 livestream, Bonnie said the controversy was taking a toll on her, particularly because of its impact on her friends.“Trying to use me and attack my friends. Specifically Cinna. The thing is, it doesn't bother my friends as much as it really bothers me; it's starting to really eat away at me. A little bit. Because I get it; there's nothing that I can do about anything from 10 to 12 years ago. There are so many reaches that people are trying to make. Not even just to attack me; they're using me as a vessel to attack people that I love the most.”Bonnie also drew criticism after telling an elderly couple to move during a March 2026 St. Patrick's Day livestream.She later accused clipping channels of deliberately seeking drama around her. The incidents have kept Bonnie in the spotlight, with old recordings and livestream moments continuing to fuel debate among viewers.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: US News: The White House on Monday launched ‘TRUMP TV: The Essentials Station’, a 24/7 digital video stream featuring administration announcements, presidentia.
articles.body: The White House on Monday launched ‘TRUMP TV: The Essentials Station’, a 24/7 digital video stream featuring administration announcements, presidential remarks and other content, as the Trump administration faces a legal challenge from CNN, MS NOW and Politico over their exclusion from the White House.The White House said the new service would bring the administration's "biggest moments" together in one place, with content updated in real time. The stream was launched on the White House's YouTube channel at 7 pm ET on Monday.The launch came hours after CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit against the Trump administration, seeking to restore their access to the White House. The organisations argue that the administration's decision to revoke their journalists' credentials violates their First Amendment rights.Trump had barred the three outlets from the White House after criticising their coverage. Their reporters were denied entry to the White House grounds on Saturday and had their press credentials confiscated, according to the organisations.CNN was also removed from its scheduled television pool duties. ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC subsequently joined CNN in suspending their participation in the White House television pool after CNN was removed from a scheduled assignment.The television pool normally provides shared video coverage of presidential events to broadcasters and other news organisations. With the pool disrupted, the White House's own video feed has become a more prominent source of footage from presidential events.Trump on Monday sharply criticised the three organisations in a social media post after they sued his administration."As expected, Fake News CNN, Politico (Pay back the 8 Million Dollar contribution made by the U.S. Government to keep them afloat!), and MSNOW (formerly known as MSDNC!), have brought suit to gain access to the White House, and your President, ME! They have drawn a great Judge, for them, a man who ruled in favor of Jim Acosta, who now seems to have disappeared from the Planet. The Judge’s name is Tim Kelly, and he was, sadly, appointed by “TRUMP.” In other words, almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal because Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown “sources,” shouldn’t be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World. It is called the Oval Office, and it should be treated with Decorum, Respect, and Dignity, not defiled by Third Rate Clowns, who purposefully distort, twist, and degrade with everything they write or publish. Virtually every story about me, or anything having to do with me, is negative, wrong and, in many cases, DANGEROUS for our Country! No matter how GREAT my Achievements, they trivialize and demean. The fact is, I won all seven Swing States, the Popular Vote, the Electoral College (312 to 226), and the Counties throughout America by 86%, and yet it is reported that I get 94% bad publicity. With such a Crooked and Corrupt Press, how did I win in such a LANDSLIDE? It is because the Media has NO credibility, and that is a very bad thing for our Nation! Why should I have to give “access” to such people? Perhaps Judge Kelly could explain that! In any event, I have an obligation to fight for the Success and Safety of our Country. FAKE NEWS IS A THREAT TO DEMOCRACY, and I will do whatever is necessary to make sure that the U.S.A. thrives."The three organisations said their lawsuit was intended to defend their First Amendment rights and the principle that the government should not decide what the press reports."This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," the outlets said in a joint statement.The case has been assigned to US District Judge Timothy Kelly, who was appointed by Trump during his first term. Kelly previously handled CNN reporter Jim Acosta's legal challenge after the White House revoked his press access in 2018.CNN, MS NOW and Politico have asked the court to restore their access while the case proceeds. A hearing on their request is scheduled for Wednesday.The dispute centres on whether the administration can restrict journalists' access to the White House based on objections to their reporting. articles.title: US plans to reopen two military sites in Greenland: Report
articles.summary: US News: The United States plans to reopen a former Cold War-era military base in southern Greenland and establish a military presence at an eastern Greenland .
articles.body: The United States plans to reopen a former Cold War-era military base in southern Greenland and establish a military presence at an eastern Greenland outpost currently used by Denmark's Sirius Dog Sled Patrol, according to report by Reuters.The move is expected to be part of a new security agreement between the United States, Denmark and Greenland that the three sides are expected to sign on Tuesday on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.The sites are Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland, where the US operated the Bluie West One military base until the 1950s, and Mestersvig on Greenland's east coast, which is currently used by the Sirius Dog Sled Patrol, a Danish special forces unit, two of the sources said.The agreement is expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly in New York at 10:30 a.m. ET (1430 GMT) on Tuesday.The text of the agreement has not been made public. The sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said its details had not been finalised and could change before the signing.The governments of Denmark and Greenland did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The White House also did not immediately respond.Deal follows Trump's pressure over GreenlandThe agreement comes after months of pressure from US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly said he wants the United States to control Greenland and has at times declined to rule out using military or economic force to acquire the semi-autonomous Danish territory.Trump's threats, which intensified in January, triggered a diplomatic crisis within NATO and led Denmark and Greenland to negotiate with Washington in an effort to ease tensions.Denmark has said the new agreement would place Arctic security within the framework of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization rather than leave responsibility solely with the United States and Denmark.US military presence in GreenlandThe United States maintained a much larger military presence in Greenland during the Cold War, operating 17 military installations and deploying more than 10,000 personnel there.Today, only Pituffik Space Base remains as a US military installation in Greenland, with around 150 US military personnel.The planned return to Narsarsuaq and presence at Mestersvig would expand the US military footprint on the strategically important Arctic island, although the precise scale and nature of the deployments were not immediately clear.Greenland is a semi-autonomous territory of Denmark and occupies a strategically important position between North America and Europe. Its location also makes it important for monitoring activity in the Arctic and the North Atlantic.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 4 European nations back India's bid for permanent UN seat, Jaishankar calls it 'historic'
articles.summary: India News: Poland, Hungry, Slovakia and Czech Republic on Monday backed India's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, with Slovakia fo.
articles.body: Poland, Hungry, Slovakia and Czech Republic on Monday backed India's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, with Slovakia foreign minister Juraj Blanár saying India, as a leading country of the Global South and an emerging power in the Indo-Pacific, should have a place at the UN's top decision-making body.The remarks came after external affairs minister S Jaishankar participated in the first high-level Visegrád Group (V4) plus India meeting on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York."We all agree, as V4 countries, that India, as part of the Global South, an upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be at the table as a permanent member of the UN Security Council," Blanár said.The V4 comprises Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia. The four countries held their first ministerial-level meeting with India in the new V4+India format during the UNGA high-level week.Jaishankar described the meeting as a "new historic occasion" and said the discussions covered political, economic, defence, technology, space, connectivity and people-to-people ties."We had our first Visegrad Four and India meeting. It was, in a sense, a new historic occasion, and I would like to thank Minister Juraj (Foreign Minister of Slovakia) for convening us today. It was a very, very productive meeting. What we agreed was that since India's relationship with the European Union itself is deepening, with the V4, we would take some special initiatives to create an annual business forum. As foreign ministers, we would meet annually. That was the consensus. We would also explore in technology and innovation whether we could be doing more. We have a very strong history with all the V4 countries in defense. We want to refresh and take forward that record and that cooperation. We discussed space issues, connectivity, and people-to-people mobility. We have students in each of the V4 countries. Overall, in terms of our cooperation, as well as a very good and useful exchange on the big global crisis, the Ukraine conflict, and what's happening in the Gulf. I think it was a very worthwhile and productive meeting. I'm very pleased about it."Jaishankar on V4's role in global affairsAsked about the political importance of the V4 for India on the global stage, Jaishankar said New Delhi viewed the four countries as partners with strong industrial, technological and innovation capabilities."We have very good relations with the V4 countries, and we know that these are countries with a very strong, very distinctive capability. They are industrial economies, economies with great innovation and technology talent. And I think how the V4 come together is for them to decide. But we certainly welcome the opportunity to work."India has been seeking reform of the UN Security Council and a permanent seat on the body. The Council currently has five permanent members, China, France, Russia, the UK and the US, alongside 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms.Jaishankar had formally launched India's campaign for a non-permanent UNSC term for 2028-29 in July, while New Delhi has continued to press for broader reform of the Council and permanent membership for India.India, V4 agree on closer cooperationJaishankar said the meeting also resulted in an agreement to strengthen cooperation through annual foreign ministerial meetings and an annual business forum.In a post on X, Jaishankar said: "Our first meeting in the V4+India format agreed to: Closer political cooperation including annual meetings of Foreign Ministers. Deeper economic cooperation, including the Annual Business Forum. Reinvigorating our defence cooperation. Further development of our cultural cooperation and people-to-people relations."The meeting included Poland's deputy prime minister and foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, Hungary's deputy prime minister and foreign minister Dr Anita Orbán, Slovakia's foreign minister Juraj Blanár and Czechia's foreign minister Petr Macinka.Jaishankar is leading the Indian delegation at the 81st UN General Assembly high-level week in New York and is scheduled to address the General Debate on September 26.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Pro-Putin party wins big, sweeps Russian elections
articles.summary: Europe News: MOSCOW: The pro-Putin ruling United Russia party won a record number of seats in the national parliament, according to near-complete official election.
articles.body: MOSCOW: The pro-Putin ruling United Russia party won a record number of seats in the national parliament, according to near-complete official election results on Monday, while the anti-war Yabloko party appeared to have won a tiny foothold in one regional parliament.President Vladimir Putin had cast the three-day election to State Duma –– the first since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in Feb 2022 –– as a test of support for the war. Elections for some regional parliaments and governors were held at the same time. In a tightly controlled political system, which critics say does not tolerate genuine dissent and under which many of Yabloko’s candidates were barred, few surprises were expected.But political analysts said it was important to the authorities that the process itself was seen to be relatively smooth. Officials had cast the vote as a way of showing enemies that Russia was united.With over 95% of the vote counted, Ella Pamfilova, chair of the Central Electoral Commission, said United Russia had scored 57.83%, up from the 49.8% that it won in the last parliamentary election, in 2021. United Russia was set to control 355 seats or nearly 80% of the 450-seat Duma, a total that includes results in individual constituencies. That would maintain its constitutional majority –– enabling it to pass laws and initiate amendments to the constitution without the support of other parties. It would also be an all-time high, outstripping its 2016 record of 343 seats.Four other parties had made it into parliament –– the Communists with 13.81%, the ultra-nationalist LDPR with 8.98% and the New People party with 7.96%. The Just Russia party narrowly made the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament. All of those parties have voted in the same way as United Russia on major issues in recent years. Yabloko, the only registered anti-war party, failed to win any seats at a national level.In Chechnya, Ramzan Kadyrov, a close Putin ally, was re-elected to a fifth term as leader with an official tally of near 100%. Pamfilova said turnout among Russia’s 111 million voters, which she put at 59.3%, was a record for such an election, which continued despite a heavy Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow on Sunday.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Amazon blocks Meta's AI Agent Muse AI on its app, unhappy with Facebook-parent capturing and storing customer credentials; says, 'never told us that ...'
articles.summary: Tech News News: Amazon has reportedly blocked Meta’s new autonomous personal assistant, Muse, from navigating and purchasing products on Amazon.com on behalf of shopp.
articles.body: Amazon has reportedly blocked Meta’s new autonomous personal assistant, Muse, from navigating and purchasing products on Amazon.com on behalf of shoppers. The restriction follows unsuccessful attempts by the retail giant to convince Facebook’s parent company to voluntarily drop Amazon from the artificial intelligence (AI) tool’s automated shopping routines. Last year, Amazon sent a cease-and-desist letter to Perplexity, asking the company to stop their bots and that the e-tailer does not want to be part of Comet browser.GeekWire reported that Amazon said it never consented to the integration. It added that Meta launched the feature without advance notice, designed the agent to browse without identifying itself as automated software, and appears to harvest and retain customer credentials, a combination Amazon warns poses serious privacy and security hazards.By Sunday (September 20) night, consumers attempting to use Muse for purchases on Amazon encountered an explicit roadblock message: “Continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use, to which our customers have agreed.”According to the report, an Amazon spokesperson emphasized that external platforms should adhere to basic commercial boundaries:“We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate.”Meta’s position on credential securityMeta has previously rejected allegations that its agent mishandles sensitive user information. The parent company of Facebook and Instagram noted that Muse operates without direct visibility into user passwords or banking details. It also stated that any log-in information entered by a consumer is placed into protected storage, enabling the model to utilise credentials without reading them directly, even when an individual types them straight into a browser session.The clash creates an awkward rift between two longstanding commercial allies. Since 2023, Amazon has allowed consumers to buy products directly within Facebook and Instagram feeds. In April, Meta inked a multibillion-dollar contract to run its autonomous AI agents using Amazon's custom Graviton server chips.The report said that the friction exposes a wider battle over which tech firm maintains ownership of the shopper relationship as automated agents begin executing digital commerce on behalf of people.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: 'Illegally entered': ICE agent shoots Venezuelan man in Texas- watch
articles.summary: US News: A Venezuelan national shot and wounded by a US immigration agent in Texas was transferred to an ICE detention centre with the bullet still lodged in h.
articles.body: A Venezuelan national shot and wounded by a US immigration agent in Texas was transferred to an ICE detention centre with the bullet still lodged in his body, his lawyer said Monday.Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, said he was delivering a DoorDash order in Austin on Sunday when an ICE agent allegedly rammed his vehicle and shot him."I'm in a lot of pain because the shot fractured my clavicle and at the hospital where they took me they couldn't remove the bullet because it's close to the spinal cord...I'm not doing very well, I still have the bullet inside," Perez told reporters by phone.The shooting is the latest instance of violence involving Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents enforcing President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown, AFP reported.Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said on X that Perez had "illegally entered our country under the Biden administration and had a final order of removal". His attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, disputed that account, saying Perez was in the US legally with a work permit.Lincoln-Goldfinch said Perez was transferred from a hospital to an ICE detention centre in Pearsall, about 135 miles (215 km) southwest of Austin."He was shot here in his back, and they didn't take the bullet out, and they didn't give him pain medication, and they transferred him to ICE, to a processing center where he spent the night without a bed," she said.Perez disputes account of shootingPerez said a truck pulled up alongside his vehicle while he was on his way to deliver the order and tried to hit him without using lights or sirens.He said a black pickup then cut him off and an agent got out and demanded his documents. Perez said he asked to pull over from the middle of the road but the agents refused."I made a U-turn and that's when he started chasing me, thinking I was going to run away, but I was looking for a place to leave my car safely," he said."That's when he hit me twice and shot me."Perez said he did not know how many shots were fired.After the shooting, an ambulance took him to hospital, where he said doctors initially ran tests in preparation for surgery to remove the bullet. He alleged that the procedure was later halted because agents were in a hurry to discharge him and transfer him to detention.Lincoln-Goldfinch alleged that there was "absolutely zero justification" for the shooting and called for an end to ICE traffic stops.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Why do students study more under pressure but remember less?
articles.summary: Every exam season, the same scene repeats itself in homes across India. Lights stay on past midnight, notebooks pile up, and a student who has barely .
articles.body: Every exam season, the same scene repeats itself in homes across India. Lights stay on past midnight, notebooks pile up, and a student who has barely looked at a chapter all year suddenly spends twelve hours a day buried in it. And yet, when results come in, the outcome is often disappointing. Not because the child didn't work hard enough, but because working harder under panic and working smart under calm are two completely different things and we keep confusing one for the other.The Panic-Study TrapWhen pressure mounts, it has been seen that many students do not make productive use of their study time and only extend the time spent with books, rather than effectively improving learning. Time spent just looking at pages while being anxious about the limited time available is not going to help to learn anything. Students convince themselves they are very busy and making progress, but the reality is that their brains are not functioning in a way that allows for the retention of any new information.What Pressure Actually Does to the BrainIt’s not merely a case of study techniques; it is a neurological issue. The release of cortisol in the body during times of stress has an impact on the function of the hippocampus – the area of the brain that processes learning and storage of information. This is the reason behind why you can read the same portion of text several times right before the exam and still remember nothing the next day. The brain was preoccupied with fighting anxiety rather than remembering facts. While it may be possible for short-term stress to improve focus, chronic and severe stress is counterproductive in that it decreases retention of information.Cramming Feels Like Learning. It Isn't.There's also a simpler, more familiar culprit: cramming. Reading something once under deadline pressure creates a false sense of familiarity. The material feels recognisable, so the brain assumes it's learned. But recognition and recall are not the same skill, and exams almost always test recall. Real memory needs repetition spaced out over days, not hours something most students only discover the hard way, usually a night too late."Children rarely fail because they didn't try hard enough. They fail because the last few days before an exam are treated as the only days that matter," says Mr Rishi Pal Chauhan, the Architect for Personalised Learning, Founder & Director, Jiva Group.What Actually HelpsFixing the issue is straightforward, although putting it into practice is more difficult. Spreading studying out over many weeks instead of cramming all the information into one session lets the brain become familiar with the material gradually which is exactly what is needed to help memorize it. Taking short breaks, sleeping well, or doing a little bit of exercise can help with lowering cortisol and allow the hippocampus to perform its functions. Testing oneself on the material that he/she is trying to learn creates much stronger connections in the brain than just going over the material.However, it does not mean that pressure should be absent. A certain level of pressure can motivate students to study, but when the pressure becomes the only factor motivating them to study, the stress can hinder their performance.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: In 2012, Holly the Florida house cat fled after fireworks, survived a 190-mile journey and was reunited with her owners 62 days later
articles.summary: US News: A house cat named Holly disappeared during a Florida holiday in late 2012 after fireworks frightened her and she bolted from her owners' motor home. J.
articles.body: A house cat named Holly disappeared during a Florida holiday in late 2012 after fireworks frightened her and she bolted from her owners' motor home. Jacob and Bonnie Richter had travelled with Holly to the Daytona International Speedway, about 190 miles from their home in West Palm Beach. The family searched for the missing cat and distributed flyers before eventually returning home without her. Sixty-two days later, Holly was found in a Palm Beach Gardens garden, emaciated and weak. A veterinarian scanned her for a microchip, leading to her owners being contacted. The indoor cat had made her way back towards home.Florida cat Holly disappeared after fireworksThe Richters had taken Holly with them on their road trip when she became separated from them. The ABC News report said she was "spooked by fireworks" and bolted from the motor home, leaving her owners searching for her in the area around Daytona International Speedway.The family continued looking for Holly before they had to leave without her. They handed out flyers and contacted local agencies during their search, but the cat could not be found at the time. The Richters eventually returned to their home in West Palm Beach without knowing what had happened to her.Holly was found weak after 62 daysSixty-two days later, a woman named Barb Mazzola found an emaciated cat in her yard in Palm Beach Gardens. According to ABC News, the cat was "so skinny, all bones and weak" and could "hardly walk". Mazzola bought food for the animal and took her to a veterinarian on a Saturday.At the veterinary clinic, Holly was scanned for a microchip. The identification allowed the veterinarian to establish who the cat belonged to, leading to the Richters receiving a call informing them that Holly had been found.Holly was found just one mile from homeThe Richters were shocked to learn that Holly had survived and made her way back to the area where they lived. According to the ABC News report, she was found only one mile from the family's home in West Palm Beach.Jacob Richter described the journey to ABC News affiliate WPBF-TV as "quite a journey for this little girl". He added: "We just can't believe she came home." The discovery meant that Holly had returned to the vicinity of her home after disappearing during the family's trip to Daytona.Indoor cat Holly travelled 190 miles homeHolly's return was particularly notable because she was an indoor cat and had travelled a long distance after becoming separated from her owners. Veterinarian Marty Becker told ABC News that animals have a sense of direction, but said it was unusual for cats to find their way home over long distances."All animals have a sense of direction," Becker said, according to the ABC News report, adding that it was "really unusual for cats to find a way home over long distances". Holly had covered the roughly 190 miles between Daytona and the Richters' home.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1978, 13-year-old Jacob Arabo’s father gifted him a watch; years later, his creations adorned A-list wrists: ‘I had to stop being a workman’
articles.summary: US News: Cristiano Ronaldo, Jay-Z, Kanye West, and David Beckham have all been photographed wearing Jacob & Co.’s now-iconic Five Time Zone watch. The bran.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo, Jay-Z, Kanye West, and David Beckham have all been photographed wearing Jacob & Co.’s now-iconic Five Time Zone watch. The brand’s name has also long been intertwined with A-listers, with a language of diamonds, gold and “bling”. But before Jacob & Co. became a name associated with elaborate timepieces, its founder Jacob Arabo was a teenager in Tashkent who had become fascinated by a watch his father gave him.He was 13 when his father, Nison, gifted him a dual-time watch. The boy was captivated by the mechanism and the idea of displaying different time zones. That childhood fascination would return decades later, when Arabo created the Five Time Zone watch. “I was fascinated by it. I think this is what led me to develop the Five Time Zone watch, that really started our watchmaking journey,” Arabo recalled in an interview with WorldTempus.From Tashkent to New YorkBorn in 1965 in Tashkent, then part of the Soviet Union, Arabo grew up in a Bukharian Jewish family. His father had been involved in manufacturing and distributing liquor, but after the family moved to the US in 1979, he struggled to find work and support the family.Arabo eventually left high school at 17 to help his family financially. “My father was an educated man… But at the time under the Soviet regime, there weren’t many opportunities to have a better life. So, in 1979, he decided to bring our family (from Tashkent, Uzbekistan) to America,” Arabo told Revolution Watch. “He found that his prospects were a lot more limited. He tried really hard to find work. But he really had trouble making ends meet, and so, at 17, I dropped out of high school to help support my family.”The teenager then enrolled in a jewellery-making course. It was meant to last six months; he completed it in four. He went on to work in a jewellery factory, but the repetitive nature of the job soon pushed him towards designing his own pieces.“I was always curious about design,” he said, explaining that he wondered why two objects made from the same materials could look so different. He also became interested in photography and the role of perspective, detail and lighting in making something beautiful.Then came a small opportunity that changed the direction of his life. At the factory, Arabo noticed leftover gold tubing being discarded as scrap. He turned it into a bracelet- and it sold well. “I soon realized that to really support my family, I had to stop being a workman and start being a jeweler myself,” he said.Still only 17, he opened his own factory near New York’s Diamond District. He would spend four days working on designs and the remaining three visiting department stores to sell them. By 1986, at 21, he had opened his own jewellery shop on Sixth Avenue.How Jacob became ‘Jacob the Jeweler’It took years before Arabo developed a following among New York’s hip-hop community. His jewellery was different from the conventional designs of the time: larger, more conspicuous and created around the tastes of a new generation of artists who were beginning to command both cultural and financial influence.The late rapper The Notorious B.I.G. eventually gave him the name that would stick- “Jacob the Jeweler”. Arabo's work and name then began appearing in hip-hop culture, including references in songs by Jay-Z, 50 Cent, Beyoncé, Big Sean, Rick Ross, A$AP Ferg and Kanye West.Arabo had a simple explanation for why artists kept coming back. “The reason I think they all came to me was, firstly, I always treated them with respect. As a young person, I genuinely admired what they did. I admired their success,” he said. He also wanted to create what they wanted, but with the best craftsmanship and stones he could provide. That relationship between Arabo and the music world would eventually help take Jacob & Co. far beyond New York’s Diamond District.The watch that changed Jacob & Co.In 2002, Arabo launched the Five Time Zone watch- a design that combined the bold, gem-set aesthetic associated with his jewellery with multiple time displays.The watch quickly became a fixture in celebrity and hip-hop culture. Jay-Z, Kanye West, Busta Rhymes, Nigo, Pharrell Williams, Bono, David Beckham and Leonardo DiCaprio were among those photographed wearing it, according to Revolution Watch. Later, A$AP Rocky, A$AP Ferg, Romeo Beckham and Drake were also spotted wearing versions of the watch.But there was an interesting contradiction at the heart of its success: the original Five Time Zone was quartz-driven. For Arabo, the popularity of the watch was not the end of his watchmaking ambitions. It was the beginning.“When I get interested in a subject, I love to do research, I love to learn,” he said. He began studying traditional complications and high watchmaking and spent increasing amounts of time in Switzerland.From bling to high watchmakingIn 2007, Arabo introduced the Quenttin, his first major venture into high watchmaking. The watch featured seven mainspring barrels and a vertical tourbillon. Its design reflected Arabo’s growing interest in making watches that were not simply decorative, but technically ambitious.The Quenttin also taught him what he wanted from future creations. “I wanted to make these kinds of super complications but in a way that was personally meaningful to me,” he said. “Even if I was to work with the best high complications specialists, the movements had to be exclusive to me.”That ambition led to the Epic SF24 in 2013, inspired partly by the split-flap information boards Arabo remembered seeing at airports and railway stations as a child. The watch displayed 24 cities and their corresponding time zones. But the watch that most clearly announced Arabo's new direction was the Astronomia, unveiled in 2014.The Astronomia momentArabo wanted the Astronomia to look unlike a conventional watch. He imagined something connected to space, three-dimensional and open enough for the wearer to see the movement from different angles.“I knew that watches were evolving, and I wanted to create something that was totally unique. I wanted something related to space, something that was completely three-dimensional and something with a case that was totally open so that you could see the movement from every angle,” he said.The resulting Astronomia featured a rotating four-arm carriage, a triple-axis tourbillon, a floating time display, a 288-facet diamond and a miniature globe. Arabo described the experience of wearing it as “visual poetry”.It represented a striking shift: the man who had become famous for creating the watches and jewellery loved by hip-hop stars was now pursuing increasingly complex mechanical watchmaking.And yet, the two sides of his career were not as disconnected as they might appear.Arabo has said that he wanted Jacob & Co. to create watches that were visually spectacular while retaining authenticity in their watchmaking. “While I wanted to make the wildest, most ambitious watches possible,” he said, “it was important to me that from a watchmaking perspective, we always retained our authenticity in our approach.”A family story at its heartFor all the celebrity names associated with Jacob & Co., Arabo's own story keeps returning to family. His son Benjamin Arabov became CEO of Jacob & Co. in 2021. In an interview with Revolution Watch, Benjamin recalled his father as someone who made time for his sons and spoke enthusiastically about watches at home.Arabo, too, has spoken about family as one of his greatest rewards. “To me, this is the greatest reward in life- to have a family that still enjoys spending time together so much,” he said.There is, then, a quiet symmetry to Arabo's journey. The story that began with a teenage boy studying the watch his father had given him eventually became one of the world's most recognisable luxury watch and jewellery names.The celebrities may have helped put Jacob & Co. on the global stage. But long before the red carpets, music videos and elaborate mechanical creations, there was a young immigrant in New York trying to support his family- and a boy in Tashkent who simply wanted to understand what made a watch tick.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: How Puducherry offers housing sites to homeless and underprivileged communities
articles.summary: News News: Homelessness continues to affect many economically weaker families across Puducherry, particularly those from scheduled caste and other backward class.
articles.body: Homelessness continues to affect many economically weaker families across Puducherry, particularly those from scheduled caste and other backward class communities who lack the means to own even a piece of land to build a home on. To address this, the Union Territory administration has, over the decades, run welfare schemes aimed at helping such families secure a site of their own. One such scheme is the Distribution of Free House Sites to Scheduled Caste/Other Economically Backward Classes, launched in 1981 by the Adi Dravidar Welfare Department, government of Puducherry.Under the scheme, homeless poor scheduled caste people and other economically backward class people who meet the eligibility criteria are provided free housing sites to enable them to construct their own houses.Eligibility and documents requiredThe applicant must be a citizen of India and a native or permanent resident of the Union Territory of Pondicherry. The annual family income should not exceed Rs 24,000, and the applicant must be at least 18 years old. The applicant should be homeless, with no family member owning a house or house site, and must have a bonafide intention to construct a house within two years.Documents required include proof of identity, residence-cum-nativity certificate, income certificate, caste certificate, ration card for address proof, and certification from the revenue department stating the applicant's non-ownership of a house.Application processInterested applicants must visit, during office hours, the office or sub-office of the adi dravidar eelfare and scheduled tribes welfare department, and request a hard copy of the prescribed application form from the director, adi dravidar welfare department, Thattanchavady, Puducherry.The applicant should fill in all mandatory fields, paste a passport-size photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). The duly filled and signed form, along with the documents, should be submitted to the concerned authority, and a receipt or acknowledgment should be requested, containing essential details such as the date and time of submission and a unique identification number, if applicable.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: South Korea proposes nuclear freeze with Kim Jong Un in exchange for sanctions relief: Report
articles.summary: Rest of World News: South Korean president Lee Jae Myung has urged US president Donald Trump to seek a nuclear freeze deal with North Korea instead of insisting on immedi.
articles.body: South Korean president Lee Jae Myung has urged US president Donald Trump to seek a nuclear freeze deal with North Korea instead of insisting on immediate denuclearisation, arguing that sanctions have failed to stop North Korea from expanding its weapons programmes.In an interview with the New York Times, Lee said Washington could offer sanctions relief in exchange for Pyongyang halting further development of nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missile technology.“I believe there is significant value in a trade-off between sanctions –– which are not particularly effective anyway –– and a stop to the development of additional nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missile technology,” Lee told NYT.Lee argued that demanding complete denuclearisation under current circumstances would achieve little, as North Korea has continued to expand its nuclear capabilities while strengthening ties with Russia and China.“Aiming for denuclearisation under the current circumstances guarantees that nothing will be accomplished,” he said.Why Lee wants a nuclear freeze firstLee’s proposal would make a nuclear freeze the first step, followed by reciprocal incentives and concessions aimed at building trust with Pyongyang. He said the longer-term goal would be to create conditions in which North Korea feels secure enough to eventually reduce and give up its nuclear arsenal.The South Korean president believes Trump is uniquely positioned to restart talks with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, given the two leaders’ previous personal diplomacy. Trump met Kim three times during his first term, including a 2019 meeting at the inter-Korean border, but those talks failed to produce an agreement.Lee said the alternative to diplomacy was increasingly risky as North Korea continued to expand its nuclear arsenal.“Our estimates suggest that North Korea is now capable of producing, or may already be producing, an additional 10 to 20 nuclear weapons each year,” he said, warning that Pyongyang could eventually be tempted to export nuclear weapons and missiles for money.North Korea has more leverage nowLee’s push comes as North Korea has moved closer to Russia and China and become less dependent on negotiations with Seoul or Washington.Pyongyang has deployed troops and weapons to support Russia’s war in Ukraine, strengthening its relationship with Moscow. North Korea has also deepened ties with Beijing, while its economy has shown signs of growth.That has given Kim more room to resist pressure from Washington. North Korea has also continued developing its nuclear and missile capabilities despite Trump’s efforts to revive diplomacy.North Korea has also been regularly carrying out military exercises and testing its arsenal of ballistic missiles near South Korean waters, worsening tensions in a region already plagued by military tensions and a long-running standoff between the two Koreas.Trump had also recently scaled back a major US-South Korean military exercise, describing such drills as hostile toward Kim. North Korea has nevertheless continued weapons activity, including recent ballistic missile launches.Lee is not alone in arguing for a shift towards a phased approach. Stephen E Biegun, who served as the US special representative for North Korea during Trump’s first term, recently said Washington could negotiate a “slowing or freezing” of North Korea’s nuclear arsenal.But North Korea has repeatedly signalled that it does not intend to give up its nuclear arsenal, making any freeze deal potentially difficult to negotiate.Lee nevertheless believes a freeze would be a more realistic starting point than demanding complete denuclearisation at the outset.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Chhitputh ghatna hoti rehti hai’: Bihar minister's remarks on Jamui harassment case triggers row
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Bihar minister Shrawon Kumar has drawn criticism for describing the harassment of a minor girl in Bihar’s Jamui as 'Chhitputh' (isolated) i.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bihar minister Shrawon Kumar has drawn criticism for describing the harassment of a minor girl in Bihar’s Jamui as 'Chhitputh' (isolated) incident while asserting that the world is not entirely free from crime.He said, "These isolated incidents happen. Those who commit such acts in Bihar cannot escape; strict action has been taken against them in the past as well."The remarks came after the assault and groping of the girl, who was returning from a coaching class with a male friend, came to light through a video that went viral on social media. An FIR has been registered in connection with the incident, while police have arrested three people and formed a special investigation team to identify and apprehend others involved.JD(U) state president Umesh Kushwaha also called the incident 'chhitputh' asserting that law-and-order situation was far worse in the state before 2005, when the NDA came to power, triggering a political row.“When such ‘isolated/minor (chhitput ghatna)’ incidents happen, our administration takes quick action. But one should recall what was the state of affairs on the law and order front before 2005, when people used to live under fear and nobody used to venture out,” Kushwaha said while talking to reporters.Tejashwi attacks JD(U) RJD leader and state LoP Tejashwi Prasad Yadav criticised Kushwaha for describing the incident as isolated and called it a “blot” on Bihar.“It is really sad they are calling the assault on the girl and boy as isolated. Had the same happened with any family member of any leader, would they have said the same thing? The harassment incident is shameful,” Yadav said.Yadav alleged that “goonda raj” was prevailing in Bihar and accused the state government of attempting to suppress incidents instead of taking action against those responsible.He also questioned the government’s claims about women’s safety in the state, saying the Jamui incident showed that girls were not safe despite assertions that women could move around freely during the day and at night.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'World is getting worse': Antonio Guterres warns wars, divisions are paralysing UN
articles.summary: Rest of World News: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has warned that the global situation is deteriorating as wars spread and become increasingly complicated, with d.
articles.body: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has warned that the global situation is deteriorating as wars spread and become increasingly complicated, with deep divisions among major powers leaving the Security Council unable to respond effectively to growing crises.Speaking to Al Jazeera on Monday, a day before delivering his final address to the UN General Assembly as secretary-general, Guterres said the world body was facing serious challenges over its ability to deal with conflicts and uphold international law.'Environment of impunity'Guterres said the involvement of major powers and permanent members of the UN Security Council in conflicts had made it harder for the council to act.He said repeated violations of international law were contributing to a broader sense that countries could act without facing consequences."That creates an environment of impunity, in which midsize powers believe that they can do whatever they want because nothing will happen to them," Guterres said.According to the UN chief, geopolitical divisions have effectively paralysed the Security Council at a time when the number of conflicts is growing.He warned that the consequences were being felt most severely by vulnerable populations caught up in wars and economic disruption.Wars driving food and fuel costsGuterres pointed to the Russia-Ukraine war and the US-Israel war on Iran as conflicts with consequences far beyond the countries directly involved.He said disruptions to food, fertiliser and energy supplies were adding to pressure on economies around the world. Problems affecting key maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb, have further complicated the movement of energy and goods."The combination of the war in Ukraine with the problems of exports of foods, fertilisers, and energy through the Black Sea, if you combine it with the difficulties in the Strait of Hormuz [in the Gulf], in the Bab al-Mandeb [in the Red Sea], and in the attacks [on] oil installations in several countries of the [Middle East] region, we are creating a situation that has a devastating impact on many economies around the world," Guterres said.He said wealthier countries could eventually absorb higher interest rates and energy costs, but developing nations faced much greater difficulties.People in poorer countries, he said, were being pushed into "a desperate situation" as food and energy became more expensive and access to fertilisers became harder.UN faces pressure to reformGuterres, a former prime minister of Portugal and former UN high commissioner for refugees, has led the organisation since January 1, 2017.His second term ends on December 31, 2026, after which a new secretary-general will take charge.Guterres said his successor would inherit a UN facing multiple conflicts and a growing gap between the scale of global challenges and the organisation's ability to respond.He argued that reforms would be necessary if the UN is to remain an effective and relevant institution in a world increasingly divided by geopolitical rivalries.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: West Dallas had too few air-quality monitors to track pollution across large areas; a Plano teen built an AI model to estimate neighborhood air quality, later reaching 60 schools and training 300 youth ambassadors
articles.summary: US News: At 17, Nathan Tan has already taken on a problem that can be difficult even for adults to see, let alone solve: the invisible pollution hanging over n.
articles.body: At 17, Nathan Tan has already taken on a problem that can be difficult even for adults to see, let alone solve: the invisible pollution hanging over neighborhoods where families have spent years carrying a disproportionate share of the environmental burden. From his home in Plano, Texas, Tan has turned concern about air quality into a growing community effort that combines technology, education and grassroots action, states a report by North Texas e-News.A problem close to homeTan is the founder of Shared Skies Initiative, a nonprofit focused on environmental injustice in Dallas. His work grew out of years spent tutoring elementary school students in West Dallas, where he became increasingly aware of the area's pollution problems. His own experience with respiratory illness and the loss of family members to lung cancer also gave the issue a deeply personal dimension.A student's question about why the sky looked so hazy prompted Tan to dig deeper. He found that childhood asthma rates in West Dallas are several times the Texas average, while a single air-quality monitor covers more than 900 square miles. That left many of the communities facing the greatest risks without detailed, neighborhood-level information about the air they were breathing.Using technology to fill the gapsAs per the report, Tan initially considered expanding the network of monitoring equipment, but the cost and maintenance requirements made that approach difficult to scale. Instead, he developed a machine-learning model capable of predicting particulate matter concentrations in areas without monitoring stations. Sensor data is used to validate the model, creating a real-time air-quality map that is now used by about 1,000 Texans. The project gives residents a way to track pollution in their communities without relying solely on the limited network of traditional monitoring stations, adds the report.Taking the message into schoolsTechnology is only one part of Tan's approach. Shared Skies created a 50-page environmental justice guide in English and Spanish and distributed it to more than 60 low-income schools, reaching approximately 30,000 students. The organization has also provided 50 student-built air filters capable of reducing indoor pollution by as much as 95%, along with 10,000 KN95 masks and bilingual educational booklets. Its youth ambassador program has trained 300 young people to understand air-quality data and share practical information with their families. The effort turns students from passive recipients of environmental information into participants who can help their communities understand and respond to pollution.From classrooms to city councilsTan has also taken the issue beyond classrooms and community workshops. Shared Skies has organized letter-writing campaigns and appeared before local city councils while working with grassroots organizations to bring greater attention to air-quality concerns.One focus has been a shingle manufacturing plant located just hundreds of yards from homes in West Dallas. The organization has advocated for the plant's closure and encouraged young people to participate in local discussions about environmental policy.National recognition at 17The scale of Tan's work has now earned him national recognition. He is one of 25 recipients of the 2026 Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes, which honors young people between 8 and 18 who have made significant contributions to their communities or the environment. Fifteen of this year's winners receive $10,000 to support their service work or higher education. Tan is one of two Texas recipients this year, adds the news report.His project began with a question about hazy air and grew into an initiative combining data science, education and community organizing. At an age when most students are still deciding what direction to take, Tan has already built a project designed to give thousands of people better information about the environment around them.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
